vision: Boutique advisors at INVRT will walk into every client conversation with a cited, mandate-scoped briefing because Mandate turns the mandate's documents into defensible work product, replacing Ctrl-F and uncited chat with clickable sources and reviewed exports.
mission: Give INVRT analysts and leads one mandate-scoped workspace to ingest documents, interrogate them with citations, fill an evidence table, and export a reviewed Word briefing so partners spend time on judgment rather than document archaeology.

personas.name: Managing Partner
jobs: Approve client-ready briefings without leaking other mandates
Judge advice quality from cited evidence rather than unaudited chat
Decide build-versus-buy for research tooling with a clear internal alternative

personas.name: Mandate lead
jobs: Keep a shared fact base for the mandate
Prioritise diligence questions before the next client call
Block export until the briefing is good enough

personas.name: Analyst
jobs: Ingest CIMs, filings, and notes into one corpus
Ask questions and fill an evidence table with citations
Draft the house-template memo from the table

personas.name: Operator
jobs: Manage membership and roles on mandates
Export audit packs for any research run

epics.title: Cited document interrogation
epics.problemStatement: Analysts at boutique advisory firms struggle to interrogate CIMs, filings, and notes because generic chat and desktop search do not attach clickable sources, which results in uncited claims and slow Ctrl-F work. Today they paste fragments into consumer AI at a cost of hours per mandate and unverifiable answers.

features.title: Document ingest and citation index
requirements: User with mandate membership can upload PDF, DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX files into that mandate only
System parses documents asynchronously, writes chunks with page or section locators, and stamps tenant plus mandate ACL on every chunk
System records an ingest report listing files that failed parse and files that completed indexing
Retrieval and generation tools cannot read chunks from other mandates
acceptanceCriteria: Given a mandate with no files, when an analyst uploads a PDF, then the file appears as indexing and becomes queryable after ingest completes
Given two mandates, when a user queries mandate A, then no chunk from mandate B is returned
Given a corrupt file, when ingest fails, then the ingest report names the file and the error without blocking other files

features.title: Cited question answering
requirements: User can ask a natural-language question scoped to the current mandate corpus
System answers only with claims that include citation spans, or explicitly states the answer is not in the corpus
User can open a citation to the source locator (page or section) in the original document
User can reject a citation; rejected citations are stored on the run and cannot appear on export without a replacement
acceptanceCriteria: Given an indexed filing that states revenue, when the analyst asks for revenue, then the answer includes a citation that opens the supporting span
Given a question whose answer is absent, when the analyst asks, then the system states not in corpus rather than inventing a figure
Given a rejected citation, when the user exports later, then that citation is omitted unless replaced

features.title: Evidence table
requirements: User can create a table whose rows are topics or entities and whose columns are questions from a briefing template
System fills each cell from the mandate corpus with a short answer plus citations
User can edit cell text, mark a cell unverified, or rerun a single cell
User can export the table to XLSX or CSV including citation locators
acceptanceCriteria: Given a briefing template, when the analyst runs fill, then every cell is either filled with citations, marked not in corpus, or marked unverified
Given an edited cell, when the user exports XLSX, then the edited text is what appears in the spreadsheet
Given a 20 by 8 table, when fill runs, then the UI shows per-cell progress rather than a single blocking spinner

epics.title: Institutional work product
epics.problemStatement: Mandate leads struggle to turn research chat into a client-ready memo because generic AI produces unformatted prose without a citation appendix, which results in partners rebuilding Word documents by hand. Today they copy-paste at a cost of consistency and auditability.

features.title: Briefing memo generate and approve-to-export
requirements: User can generate a Word memo from the current evidence table plus cited Q&A using the INVRT house template
Memo includes a citation appendix mapping claims to source locators
Export to DOCX is blocked until a user with lead or partner role approves the run
Exported files are labelled as AI-assisted and human-reviewed
acceptanceCriteria: Given a filled evidence table, when an analyst generates a memo, then a DOCX preview is stored on the run without downloading yet
Given an analyst role, when they click export, then the system requires lead or partner approval
Given approval, when export completes, then the file downloads and an audit event records actor, run id, and model version

epics.title: Mandate workspace and isolation
epics.problemStatement: Managing partners struggle to let the team use AI on client files because consumer tools mix contexts and lack membership, which results in leakage risk that can end client relationships. Today they ban tools or work in unmanaged accounts.

features.title: Mandate workspace and membership ACL
requirements: User with permission can create a mandate with name, client label, and restricted flag
Only members of a mandate can list documents, run research, or view work product for that mandate
Admin can assign roles analyst, lead, partner, and admin on the mandate
Removing a member revokes retrieve and generate access immediately
acceptanceCriteria: Given a non-member, when they open a mandate URL, then they receive not found or forbidden without confirming the mandate exists
Given a restricted mandate, when a firm-wide search is attempted, then that mandate is excluded
Given membership removal, when the former member retries a prior run URL, then access is denied

epics.title: Encoded INVRT workflows
epics.problemStatement: Analysts struggle to start from a blank chat because INVRT's diligence process is not encoded, which results in inconsistent question coverage across mandates. Today each analyst improvises a checklist in a personal doc.

features.title: Diligence question list
requirements: User can run the diligence question-list workflow against the mandate corpus
System produces a structured list of questions mapped to INVRT checklist topics with citations for what is already answered and gaps for what is not
Mandate lead can prioritise, assign, or dismiss questions
Question list can be exported to DOCX or XLSX
acceptanceCriteria: Given a CIM that states customers but not churn, when the workflow runs, then churn appears as a gap and customers appear as answered with citations
Given lead dismissal of a question, when the list is re-exported, then that question is omitted or marked dismissed

epics.title: Governance, audit, and safe AI
epics.problemStatement: Operators struggle to allow AI on confidential files because there is no audit of prompts, retrieval, or model version, which results in either a blanket ban or unauditable risk. Today they cannot answer who saw what.

features.title: Audit log and export pack
requirements: System writes an immutable audit event for ingest, query, table fill, memo generate, approve, export, membership change, and delete
Each AI event stores redacted prompt metadata, model provider and version, retrieval chunk ids, actor, mandate id, and token cost
Admin can export an audit pack for a mandate or a single run within five minutes of request
Prompts and document text in logs are redacted per policy; raw secrets never persist in prompts or logs
acceptanceCriteria: Given a completed Q&A, when admin opens the run, then model version and chunk ids are visible
Given an audit export, when downloaded, then it contains events for that mandate only

features.title: No-train, injection defense, and limitation disclosure
requirements: System configuration and vendor contracts assert customer data is not used to train provider models
Uploaded documents are treated as untrusted; agent tools are allowlisted and cannot issue arbitrary network calls
UI discloses AI-assisted output and known limitations on every generate and export surface
High-risk export remains human-in-the-loop as specified in FEAT-005
acceptanceCriteria: Given a document that contains a prompt-injection attempting to call a non-allowlisted tool, when a run executes, then the tool is not invoked and the event is audited
Given the memo preview, when rendered, then AI-assisted disclosure is visible before download

capabilities: FEAT-001 Mandate workspace and membership ACL
FEAT-002 Document ingest and citation index
FEAT-005 Briefing memo generate and approve-to-export
FEAT-007 Audit log and export pack
FEAT-008 No-train, injection defense, and limitation disclosure
learningGoals: Validate that a partner will accept a Mandate memo as a starting draft on a mandate-shaped corpus
Measure whether the evidence table is the primary surface versus chat
Determine whether MVP is useful without a licensed fundamentals feed

capabilities: House-style PowerPoint outline from the briefing
One licensed fundamentals connector into a comps skeleton
SharePoint or Drive sync into the mandate corpus
learningGoals: Confirm whether artifacts without slides stall adoption

capabilities: Scheduled what-changed runs on the corpus
Optional firm-wide memory with Chinese walls
learningGoals: Prove mandate memory can compound without cross-client retrieval
